before: null (speculative decoding deactivated by default; flag absent from CMD)
after: native (built-in speculative drafter enabled; --speculative-drafter-model=native appended to CMD)
rationale: The frozen development workload is sequential, greedy (temperature 0, top_k 1) and short: six prompts of 15-27 input tokens producing 16-96 output tokens, five repetitions each. The baseline median FTGR is ~51-56 tok/s and TTFT ~41 ms, so the primary metric with room to move is decode throughput (FTGR), not prefill/scheduling latency. The one documented LLMD knob with a direct physical mechanism for raising effective decode throughput on greedy short generations is enabling a speculative drafter: a drafter proposes several tokens per target forward pass and the target verifies them, so on acceptance more than one token is produced per target step instead of exactly one. Under greedy decoding the accepted tokens are the target's own greedy tokens, so the emitted sequence should remain bit-identical to the non-speculative greedy path and preserve the golden outputs. --speculative-draft-count is intentionally left at its derived default so this remains a single semantic knob (changing both is a separate attempt per program.md). The knob is documented in llmd-help.txt (default null; 'native' selects the built-in drafter). No build, measurement or improvement is claimed here; this is a performance hypothesis only.
expected_benefit: Higher effective FTGR (tokens per second) on the short greedy decode workload, because multiple draft tokens can be confirmed per target forward pass rather than producing one token per step. TTFT is not expected to improve (prefill of short prompts is already a single chunk at --prefill-chunk-size=256) and is not expected to regress, since prefill is unchanged. Startup may increase somewhat from initializing the native drafter; this must stay under the 1.5x last-good startup hard gate. No measured benefit is asserted.
test_plan: Root builds candidate.Dockerfile and runs the frozen development-benchmark.llmd.json with the llmd_closed_thinking_v1 profile (six sequential greedy prompts, five repetitions, temperature 0, top_k 1, per-prompt max_tokens 16-96, 120s request timeout) A/B against the last-good image, measuring per-prompt median TTFT (baseline/candidate) and Etalon FTGR (candidate/baseline) with the prompt-stratified geometric-mean bootstrap (>=3% effect, 90% CI excluding 1). Correctness gates must all pass: all requests succeed, finish_reason in {stop,length}, complete output, streamed token count within tolerance of usage.completion_tokens, greedy self-consistency across repetitions, and byte-equal golden-output match against the baseline. The single cold-startup probe must be <1.5x last-good startup. A golden-output mismatch (drafter verification not preserving greedy), an OOM, or a >1.5x startup regression rejects the attempt. --speculative-draft-count is not changed (one knob only).
